lines.text: A trucker smokes leaning against his trailer, eyeing the motel with genuine curiosity.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: Last night I saw someone coming out of the bushes back there. In a hurry. Didn't get a look at the face, truth be told.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Could it have been the vagrant? Mark?

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: Could be. Though this one walked different, straighter. But what do I know, it was dark.
I make a note of it. Though half my head's already decided, with no proof, that it was Mark. I'll need to check that.

topics.displayName: Chat while waiting for the part

lines.text: Gus stirs a coffee that's gone cold, looking out the window toward the motel.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: That footprint I found in the bushes was a dress shoe, not a sneaker.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: Dress shoe? Then it's not the vagrant. Around here, the only one dressed to the nines at that hour is the motel owner.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: I'm not saying anything else, mind you. I just load trucks. But think about it.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: The part still hasn't come in. A town like this, everything takes twice as long.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: You know what struck me as strangest? The silence. After the scream, nobody came running. Like they already knew what to do.
He takes another sip of coffee and stares at the steam, like he's looking for something more to say.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: Just about done loading. Soon as I strap this down, I'm hitting the highway and not looking back.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Anything else cross your mind since we talked?

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: Just one thing. That figure I saw coming out of the bushes was walking calm. Didn't even run. A man who does something wrong and doesn't run... he's either crazy, or he knows nobody's gonna stop him.
He climbs into the cab before I can ask anything else. The engine starts up with a tired roar.
